### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4efb988a941056d6099b680924fa41807292115d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d562f112e8d859af64081afc21be9c94a6b96a8d` — the merge of head `cf3e8107b12b8e4a34a5c635546be756135d165a` into base `4efb988a941056d6099b680924fa41807292115d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d562f112e8d859af64081afc21be9c94a6b96a8d && git checkout d562f112e8d859af64081afc21be9c94a6b96a8d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4efb988a941056d6099b680924fa41807292115d cf3e8107b12b8e4a34a5c635546be756135d165a && git checkout -B drift-repro 4efb988a941056d6099b680924fa41807292115d && git merge --no-ff cf3e8107b12b8e4a34a5c635546be756135d165a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4efb988a941056d6099b680924fa41807292115d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: 80/80 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cf3e8107b12b8e4a34a5c635546be756135d165a`

Isolated at-tier review of PR #19296 (card #19184), read off the PR body, diff, commits and check runs, the card body, the `os-dev-report` comment 5749227974, and a detached worktree at the head above. The dispatching seat's conclusions were not read as inputs. Served-tier reading: this reviewer's transcript (`subagents/agent-a6a1e20fc62a4e478.jsonl`) carries 80 assistant requests, 80 of them with the harness per-request `model` stamp equal to the value `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` binds at `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs:11903`; the identifier itself is deliberately not spelled in this comment.

### ① Derived judgments

Diff vs merge-base `e6a03e6491`: 3 files, +108/−1 — `packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts` (−1, one TSDoc line), `packages/spec/src/system/job.test.ts` (+77), `.changeset/job-example-retired-id.md` (+31).

1. **Accept set: unchanged — correct.** The deleted line is inside a comment; `JobSchema` (`job.zod.ts:181-209`) is untouched, still `strictObject` with `guidance: { id: JOB_ID_RETIRED }`. Re-measured at the head: `JobSchema.safeParse` of the block as now written ⇒ accepted; the same object with `id: "job_sync_meta"` re-added ⇒ `unrecognized_keys` naming `id` with the 17.0.0 prescription (pin test 4, and mutation M1 below). `check-widening-tells --declaration no` over the real diff: 1 contract file judged, no tell; 2 NOT MEASURED by design (a test and a changeset).
2. **Public surface: unchanged — correct.** No export moves. The block never reaches `dist/*.d.ts`, and the reason is structural, not incidental: the "Job Schema" docblock (`:130-148`) is immediately followed by a second docblock (`:149-158`) for the non-exported `const JOB_ID_RETIRED`, so TypeScript attaches the example to that const, and `export const JobSchema` carries no TSDoc at all. Verified in the published 17.4.0 tarball: `grep -rl "Metadata Sync Job" package/dist` ⇒ zero files, while the fenced `defineJob` example IS present in `dist/translation.zod-*.d.ts` (positive control). Pre-existing and outside this card — carried under ③.
3. **Generated artifacts and docs: nothing derives from this block — correct.** `packages/spec/scripts/build-docs.ts` has no `@example` handling; `lib/file-description.ts` reads module-header docblocks only (this is not the file's first docblock); `check-skill-examples.ts` populates from FENCED ts/tsx blocks (this block is a bare literal, no fence); `check-yaml-examples.ts` declares TSDoc `@example` roots out of scope. `content/docs/**`, `packages/spec/json-schema/**`, `api-surface*/**`, `liveness/**`, `prompts/**`: zero hits for `Metadata Sync Job`, `sync_metadata_nightly`, `job_sync_meta`. CI on this head: `TypeScript Type Check` (the required job carrying `check:generated` and `check:docs`) ⇒ `success`.
4. **`Clause-②: no` — stands.** Deleting a key from an example cannot widen, and no derivation exists that a comment could widen through (item 3). This is not a deletion of a rejection, so no `Contract-text:` is owed; for completeness, the published contract text the example is brought into line with is the shipped tombstone (`src/system/job.zod.ts` in the 17.4.0 tarball): 「`job.id` was removed in @objectstack/spec 17.0.0 (ADR-0049) — nothing ever read it … Delete the key; rename the job via `name`」.
5. **Scope — re-derived; the card holds.** `job.zod.ts` at the head carries exactly two `@example` tags (`:134`, `:218`). Only the first carried `id`; the `defineJob` block (`:218-225`) is `name`/`schedule`/`handler` only, no retired key. Across `packages/spec/src` (203 `.zod.ts` files, 358 `@example` blocks) 11 other blocks carry an `id:` line on other schemas — not judged here: that is #19065's sweep, and this PR correctly does not start it.
6. **The pin reads the source and cannot pass vacuously — verified by mutation.** `job.test.ts` reads `./job.zod.ts` via `readFileSync(resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), './job.zod.ts'))` — same package, so no cross-package input; `vitest.repo-tests.json` does not list it, so it runs in the `local` project CI executes. At the head: 59/59. Seven mutations of the source in the worktree, each restored to a clean tree afterwards:
   - M1 re-add `id: "job_sync_meta"` ⇒ 2 fail (`parses as written`, with the `unrecognized_keys` issue list as the message; `opens with name`).
   - M2 change the anchor caption ⇒ 4 fail, the first on `toContain(ANCHOR)` — no empty-string pass.
   - M3 append prose inside the docblock after the block ⇒ 4 fail, `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'See'` — loud.
   - M4 shrink to the invalid `{ name: "x" }` ⇒ 1 fail (`invalid_type` on the required keys).
   - M5 break the closing ` */` gutter ⇒ 4 fail on extraction.
   - M6 replace with a minimal VALID job ⇒ passes. This is the pin's floor, stated so nobody reads it as a hole: the pin holds "the block parses as a job and opens with `name`", not "the block is this text" — the right invariant for this card.
   - M7 make `JobSchema` non-strict (drop `strictObject` and the guidance map) ⇒ the firing control fails (`expected true to be false`): the instrument detects its own dulling.

   `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` at the head ⇒ exit 0. `new Function` over source text is lint-clean here (no `no-new-func` / `no-implied-eval` in `eslint.config.mjs`) and confined to a test.

### ② Semver level

**`patch` on `@objectstack/spec` — correct. `skip-changeset` would be wrong; `minor` and `major` would be wrong.** Re-derived from the published artifact, not the manifest: the 17.4.0 tarball (`spec-17.4.0.tgz`, 2072 files) contains `package/src/system/job.zod.ts`, and that shipped copy carries the defective line (`:96 id: "job_sync_meta"`). So the corrected file publishes, and a false TSDoc in a shipped file is a defect in a released package (review-checklist: 「spec 发运 `src/**/*.zod.ts`,假 TSDoc/`.describe()` 即缺陷」) ⇒ a bug fix ⇒ `patch`, never `skip-changeset` (that label is for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package). Nothing is added (not `minor`); the accept set does not move (not `major`; `check-changeset-no-major` ✓, `check-empty-changeset` ✓, `Check Changeset` ✓ on this head). Changeset frontmatter `"@objectstack/spec": patch` is consistent with the PR body's `Clause-②: no` (a `no` carries no minimum level). The changeset body carries no model identifier and the diff touches no release page or CHANGELOG.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions: []`. Three `out_of_scope_findings` flagged by the dev, plus one of mine.

1. **`handler: "services/syncStatus.ts:syncAll"` — reported, deliberately not fixed. Leaving it was right; the residual is real and is owed a card.** Re-measured: `JobSchema.handler` is `z.string()` described as "Handler function name (must match a key in `defineStack({ functions })`)" (`job.zod.ts:193`); `AppPlugin` resolves `fnMap[job.handler]` (`app-plugin.ts:1220`) over `collectBundleFunctions` (`:2292`), a plain name→fn map keyed by `bundle.functions` names; the only colon-splits in runtime, cli and core are a host:port split (`cli/src/commands/serve.ts:5488`) and a hook-category split (`core/src/security/plugin-permission-enforcer.ts:345`), so no `file:export` spelling is lowered anywhere; a miss is `warn` + skip (`:1222`, pinned at `app-plugin.jobs.test.ts:275-289`). So the block copied verbatim still schedules nothing after this PR — it fails one layer later, and the card's own boundary sentence 「示例照抄即失败是 (a)」 covers it. The exemption (`.claude/agents/os-dev.md`, four conditions, all must hold): ② mechanical with a pinned shape — yes (`handler: 'syncAll'`; the sibling `defineJob` form and `examples/app-showcase` are the shape); ③ no other claim on the file — yes (`No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` ✓); ④ same gate family — satisfiable by a spelling pin in the same test file; ① same defect class — **not met, by the board's own calibration on this very card**: the #16292 implementer found the `id` defect while narrowing `timezone` and did not ride it in, and the filer endorsed that as a different defect class; by that yardstick a parse-time refusal carrying a tombstone prescription and a boot-time silent skip carrying none are two classes even inside one block. One condition down ⇒ the rule's default (list, don't touch) is exactly what happened, with dedupe words in the report. **Escalation, to the seat:** the dev has no filing budget, so that card does not exist yet — file it (class (a), naming the published surface `src/system/job.zod.ts` in the tarball; a sub-issue of #19065 or standalone) at or before landing. `Fixes #19184` is correct for the card as written — its defect statement is the parse refusal and it names nothing else — but the card's rationale is only fully discharged once the sibling card exists.
2. **`check:skill-examples` is blind to unfenced `@example` literals** — confirmed (its population is fenced ts/tsx/typescript blocks, 10 in spec sources; this block has no fence). Carrier #19065. Agree: noted, not widened here.
3. **Trailing space on the `handler` line** — pre-existing, comment-internal, read by no gate. Agree.
4. **Mine — the orphaned docblock (① item 2).** The "Job Schema" TSDoc, example included, is attached to `const JOB_ID_RETIRED`, so `JobSchema` has no hover text and the example is invisible to every declaration-based reader. Same block, same family as flag 1 — belongs on that card or on #19065; not this PR's scope and not a reason to hold it.

Independence and landing inputs: the dev was a `mode:subagent` build (branch identity below); this record is an isolated subagent's and names no session of its own. Check runs on this head, read at 2026-09-20T10:56Z (last completion 2026-09-20T10:47:48Z): 35/35 completed, none non-green; the seven required contexts (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` — 6 shards and the rollup, `Dogfood Regression Gate` — 3 shards and the rollup, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`) all `success`. No governed surface in the file list.
